item.title: Community Update #3
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
ICYMI, check out our Community Calls on YouTube or keep reading for a recap of what’s new below.

Most importantly, we launched a major protocol update on the Avalanche network with Trader Joe as our first AMM. What does this mean? We can now create leveraged exchanges on top trading pairs, like JOE-USDC and AVAX-USDC, in addition to the WETH-BTC and ETH-USDC exchanges and pools we’ve already launched on Arbitrum.

Read on to find out more about the recent product launch, updates around our community and governance, what’s next, and more:

Product

  • V4.1 — One of our most significant updates to date. Futureswap now taps into the liquidity of AMMs to create leveraged pairs, allowing traders to have leverage and manage risk on any pair listed on the underlying AMM. We’ve opened up the possibilities of doing on-chain leverage on broader, long-tail tokens as an extension of our leverage protocol with added features that make the platform significantly more flexible and composable. The protocol is currently permissioned via token governance, however, the end goal is to allow users to pemissionlessly launch leverage on any token pair on any AMM. Stay tuned for an announcement regarding our next update.
  • Celer Bridge — As part of this update, we worked with Celer so that our governance token, FST, can now be bridged one-to-one between Ethereum and Avalanche, with gas fees paid in the respective chain’s token. Notably, this is the first oracle-less bridge deployed to another L1 from Ethereum.
  • JOE-USDC — JOE is the native, on-chain token for the Trader Joe AMM, running atop the Avalanche blockchain. Naturally, it made sense to start with this pair.
  • AVAX-USDC — Similarly, as our community’s most requested pair after JOE, we enabled AVAX trading to support the Avalanche blockchain’s native token as we continue to onboard exchanges from this ecosystem.

Governance

  • Open Source — Our end goal is to provide the best possible leveraged trading experience for digital assets. That requires composability, decentralization, non-custodial liquidity, community governance, capital efficiency, economic security, and most of all — trustlessness. To further our commitment to trustlessness for traders and liquidity providers, the Futureswap code base is almost entirely open source; discover the GitHub repository here. Learn more about what’s in the repos, the respective third-party security audits, and more on our blog.
  • Liquidity Providing Risks — In order to trade with leverage on our exchange, liquidity is needed. While being incredibly safe, we dive into the risks and rewards for our liquidity providers in this post.

Community

  • Celer Twitter Space — As the first oracle-less bridge deployed to another L1 from Ethereum, we hosted a Twitter Space with the @CelerNetwork team to dive into the details. Note that Twitter is notorious for the downtime with Twitter Spaces. Check back later if you can’t listen to the recording.
  • JOE-USDC Trading Competition — To celebrate our v4.1 launch, we hosted our first ever trading competition on the JOE-USDC pair, with sweet prizes including AVAX cash and limited-edition POAPs. Be sure to let us know which pairs you’d like to see next!
  • Twitter — You may have noticed our Twitter feed has been picking up steam. Follow, tag, or mention us with what’s on your mind. This bear market is where the real work gets done; let’s connect!

Social

If you don’t follow our Twitter yet, it’s the best way to stay up to date with the latest. Here are some of of our favorite tweets:

  • Pool Together with Pooly — A lawsuit has been brought against Pool Together, a well-known DeFi application that operates a decentralized version of the UK’s Premium Bonds. The implications are wide-reaching, and could impact protocols like ours. We minted their Pooly NFT to stand in solidarity and support the defense.
  • AVAX Supply — From subnets to their validating nodes, Avalanche is approaching things differently with their chain. We addressed a theory about their possible impending supply shock, and how you could trade on Futureswap with your sentiment.
  • ETH Merge — This year looks better than ever for The Merge™, and we couldn’t be more excited. Whether you want to stack ETH in advance of then, or skeptically short it, we broke down how the development towards proof-of-stake had been going up until then. Note, it hasn’t slowed down.
  • Delta-neutral JOE — We’re big JOE fans over here, but recent macro events show you can never be too prepared for sudden downturns. We laid out a simple strategy for going ‘delta-neutral’ — that is to say, a way to strategically hedge your bets regardless of your long-term confidence.

Team

  • wilton#0626 — Wilton joined the team in March as our Director of Marketing! From writing for this blog to owning our Twitter communications, he’s been instrumental in helping us get the Futureswap word out. Give him a shout on our Discord.
  • Current Openings — If you’re reading this post, you’re likely already in the crypto community and someone we’re interested in talking to. Check out our current opportunities; we’re currently looking for a Content Writer and an Executive Assistant / Office Manager.

What’s Next

Join our 13th Community Call on Friday, June 17th, 2022 at 11am PST to learn more about where we’re going from here. Feel free to ask questions in the channel ahead of time, and stay tuned with the links below until then —

item.title: A JOE/USDC Trading Competition
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
Starting this week, register and trade on our JOE-USDC exchange for a chance to win thousands in $AVAX and POAP prizes, including a random raffle. Pre-register now.

To celebrate the launch of our v4.1 update allowing us to list any tokens atop any AMM, starting with Trader Joe’s JOE and Avalanche’s native AVAX token, we’re giving traders another reason to be excited about our new listings — a trading competition for JOE/USDC. Here’s a quick run down of the prizes and how we calculate the rankings:

Winner tiers based on P&L:

  1. $7k in $AVAX 🥇
  2. $2k in $AVAX 🥈
  3. $1k in $AVAX 🥉

Raffle specifics:

  1. $1k in $AVAX randomly sent to a non-winning registered user who opened a position 🏆

We have POAPs for early registrants, all participants and superlatives, but like the AVAX rewards above, you must be registered in order to be eligible to receive prizes.

How we calculate the rankings:

  • Your score is based on your P&L (Profit and Loss) across the whole competition period.
  • We count how much money you brought in during the competition, and how much money you took out. At the end of the competition, we evaluate your open position, if any, and interpret it as if you have closed and withdrawn the full position value.
  • Your score is basically ‘money out’ / ‘money in’.
  • If you have an open position at the start of the competition, we record the value of this position as if it were closed on the start date and time. This is considered as your initial ‘money in’ value. Otherwise, your initial ‘money in’ value is zero.
  • If you withdraw and then add some money back in later, we do not count those as “new” money. We instead subtract this amount from your ‘money out’, and only add to your ‘money in’ after your ‘money out’ becomes zero.

So, how do you register and get started?

First, check out the full Rules and Terms and Conditions. Here’s a quick TL;DR breakdown:

  • Pre-registration: Tuesday, May 24th, 11:00am PST
Head to the #🐸registration channel in our Discord and click the ‘Register’ button below the message to acknowledge the terms and receive a link via DM to the registration page. If you’re unsure about anything, please post in our #scam-reporting channel and we’ll be happy to double check the link and account. Phishers posing as our bot may try and get you to click another link — be vigilant!
  • Competition starts: Thursday, May 26th, 11:00am PST
You can still register the day the competition starts if you haven’t already.
Open a trade on the JOE/USDC exchange: x.futureswap.com/joeannounce
Keep an eye on your position on the leaderboard: https://app.futureswap.com/competition
Chat with us and other traders in the #🏆trading-competition Discord channel and on Twitter
  • Competition ends: Thursday, June 2nd, 11:00am PST.
Prize distribution: Friday, June 3rd
Keep those DMs open so we can share POAP redemption links!
On-chain funds will be sent to the winners’ addresses associated with their $JOE trades

As this is our first trading competition, feel free to send us feedback. We look forward to hosting more of these in the future, especially as we continue to onboard new pairs and trading strategies.

Good luck! 🤞

item.title: FST Goes Cross-Chain, with Native Bridging between Ethereum and Avalanche
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
Futureswap’s governance token, FST, can now be bridged one-to-one between Ethereum and Avalanche, with gas fees paid in the respective chain’s token. This is the first oracle-less bridge deployed to another L1 from Ethereum.

Given our four pair exchanges supported across Arbitrum and Avalanche, we built a path towards cross-chain governance and making FST a true multi-chain token. We partnered with the leaders in the inter-blockchain development space, Celer Network, to make this possible using their Celer Inter-Chain Message (Celer IM) framework.

Bridge now at x.futureswap.com/bridgefst

What this means

This update means cross-chain governance. Users can vote on governance proposals on Ethereum for changes on the protocol in Avalanche, and vice-versa. Soon, users will also be able to use a bridge for Arbitrum.

This is the first time, as far as we’re aware, that an oracleless bridge has been deployed to another L1 from Ethereum. Many other protocols are doing this manually, while claiming they’re doing so in a decentralized manner. Naturally, this is an attack surface, and one our bridge avoids entirely. By opening up cross-chain governance in this way, we’re expanding crypto’s ability to move across chains seamlessly, bringing the entire DeFi ecosystem closer together.

Also, there are no FST fees to transfer between Ethereum and Avalanche. Instead, the gas fees and bridge fees are paid in the native protocol token. This means that when you bridge X amount of FST on chain A, you receive X amount of FST on chain B. This helps bridgers with far more predictability on how the transaction will execute and cost.

Learn more

To help break it down and dive into the details, our CEO and co-founder, Derek Alia, will join a Twitter Space AMA with Mo Dong, the CEO of Celer Network. Join the call on Wednesday, May 4th, 2022 at 1pm PST at x.futureswap.com/celerama. You can set a reminder there, or listen to the recording if you missed it. Your only chance to ask questions will be live on the call though — we hope you can join us.

Stoked about the future of the protocol? Trade on Futureswap to earn FST rewards, own a stake, and join the community:

item.title: Launching Futureswap v4.1 on Avalanche
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
We are excited to announce the next version of Futureswap will be launched on Avalanche with Trader Joe as our first AMM! The protocol will use Trader Joe to create leveraged exchanges on the top trading pairs, including JOE-USDC and AVAX-USDC, with other pairs soon to follow.

Futureswap taps into the liquidity of AMMs to create leveraged pairs allowing traders to have leverage and manage risk on any pair listed on the underlying AMM.

Futureswap has opened up the possibilities of doing on-chain leverage on broader, long-tail tokens. The first pair to go live on our newly-integrated blockchain and AMM is JOE-USDC. Other pairs will be quickly added within the following month, with AVAX-USDC being the next supported pair. All new pairs and existing ones already live on the platform, including WBTC and ETH, can be traded with leverage.

This update is an extension of our leverage protocol with added features that make the platform significantly more flexible and composable. The protocol is currently permissioned via token governance, however, the end goal is to allow users to pemissionlessly launch leverage on any token pair on any AMM. This is the next update before that bridge is crossed.

Highlighted updates for this version:

  • Swap Adaptor — The core upgrade allows the protocol to integrate with any AMM, including Uniswap v2, Curve, Balancer, Sushi Trident, Trader Joe, and many more.
  • Token Rewards — Protocols can permissionlessly add rewards to a listed exchange pair to incentivize more activity. Futureswap is working on an interface for more easily interacting with these contracts.
  • Oracle Adaptor — The protocol can now use a Chainlink, TWAPs, or other on-chain price feeds as an oracle.
  • Frontend Redesign — Cleaner legibility improvements based on trader feedback, plus the ability to switch between chain networks while maintaining positions across multiple AMMs.
  • Multi-Chain Governance Support — By bridging contract calls, Futureswap can now operate fully decentralized across any EVM chain.
  • Gas Optimization — Code cleanup focused on quality improvement resulting in better lower gas costs.
  • Advanced Order Types — [Coming soon] As new pairs are added, exchanges will have the ability for both stop-loss and limit orders.

Futureswap v4.1 is aiming to be more aligned with token communities by giving them the ability to add leverage and more trading strategies to their token. Leverage adds utility and value to a token, but historically there has been a high barrier to get listed on leveraged exchanges. Any token that is listed on any AMM can support leverage by adding liquidity to our pools, which facilitates the leverage trading using the underlying AMM. Trading on the protocol also benefits the existing liquidity providers of an AMM pair by generating more trade fees on the pool they provide liquidity to.

What Futureswap offers:

  • Traders — Traders can now apply their strategies to the broadest range of tokens which increases profit opportunities. Currently, most protocol tokens can simply be bought and sold. Futureswap creates avenues for traders to make money by opening up leveraged longs and shorts, and with advanced trade features such as stop-loss and limit orders, users can create complex trading strategies such as delta neutral farming.
  • Liquidity Providers — Token holders can deposit to their own pool on Futureswap and earn trade fees for providing liquidity which allows traders to take on leveraged trades. Futureswap’s LP positions are at low risk of impermanent loss, generating a pool with safe yield for the token holders. Trade volume in Futureswap helps to boost the utility of the token by generating more fees for both the Futureswap pool and the respective AMM pool, thereby generating a higher APY for token holders.
  • Protocols — As a protocol, having a Futureswap exchange allows users to manage risk and take on leverage in a way that generates value for the protocol. Protocols can incentivize trade volume on their own AMM pair by providing trade rewards via Futureswap’s trade rewards system. For protocols with a treasury, or other protocol-controlled value, their token can be used as liquidity for a low-risk yield or hedging strategy.

Advantages compared to other leverage exchanges:

  • More Token Pairs — Now that the protocol can tap into any AMM pair update, users will have a greater range of pairs to select from. If there is a new token on a supported chain that the community wants, it can be quickly added to Futureswap by voting it in.
  • Co-operative Composability — By building this way, the protocol aligns traders, the underlying AMM, and token holders towards shared gain. With standard perpetuals, there’s no benefit to the token holder, as the trading is purely synthetic. On Futureswap, traders are incentivized to support the exchange given the reciprocal trade fees on their respective AMM pool and a higher APY for token holders.
  • Economic Security — The protocol has been designed to be economically safe in some key areas. Futureswap uniquely protects traders against price manipulation by using the token’s spot market as the exchange venue. The protocol uses the most liquid on-chain market for that asset and, therefore, trades are backed by the actual asset, which directly impacts the underlying AMM price.

In Futureswap, opening longs moves the spot price up, while closing them moves the price back down. Opposite to that, opening shorts moves the spot price down, and closing them moves the price back up. This means that if a malicious trader attempts to profit by opening a short on Futureswap (price go down), dumping token on spot (price go down), then closing their short (price go up), they are getting a price where they originally opened the short. While they would assume they were making a profit, they would realize the profit is coming from the spot dump — meaning they are essentially dumping on themselves.

In low-liquidity, one-sided markets traders are protected with on-chain auto-deleveraging, a rarely-used but important mechanism to compensate traders whose positions are forcibly closed (learn more here).

Lastly, you can review the most recent full audit for v4.1 here, conducted by leading security experts Trail of Bits. The audit revealed no notable issues.

Creating evolving tools of financial decentralization for permissionless markets is the primary goal through which Futureswap plans to continue growing the platform. Composably supporting all markets to continue adding more functionality for cryptocurrency traders is the foundational building block to the protocol.

item.title: Open Sourcing Futureswap
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
Another step towards full community governance

Futureswap’s end goal is to provide the best possible leveraged trading experience for digital assets. That requires composability, decentralization, non-custodial liquidity, community governance, capital efficiency, economic security, and most of all — trustlessness.

To further our commitment to trustlessness for traders and liquidity providers, the Futureswap code base is almost entirely open source; discover the GitHub repository here. Regardless of your smart contract experience, we encourage you to check out the audit reports below. Besides open-sourcing our code to minimize trust friction and increase the security of our core product, our goal is to improve Futureswap’s composability with other projects.

With access to our contracts, developers can also more easily explore building directly atop Futureswap in a variety of novel ways. For example, bots could use our API to expand trading functionality — from automatic stop-loss to placing limit orders.

The key components we’re releasing include the core contracts of version 4.1, the Command Line Interface (including the Liquidation Bot), and fs-examples (example contracts for interacting with the platform). Apart from the frontend, which we plan to open source as well, these packages make up the core of the repository.

Security is our number one priority, and we encourage you to review our most recent audit with leading security experts Trail of Bits. The audit revealed no notable issues. Ensuring a safe — not rushed — product for traders is paramount.

If you’re interested in building on top of Futureswap, we’re here to help; head to our #🛠builders channel on Discord. You can find additional documentation in our docs as well. Otherwise, if you have any questions at all, ping us on Discord or Twitter. We’re happy to dive in further.

item.title: Liquidity Provider Risks on Futureswap
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
The detailed mechanics and unique protections for the pools’ liquidity providers.

When providing liquidity in a decentralized network, trust in the underlying mechanics is paramount. Futureswap has developed a unique model for protecting the underlying funds and rewarding participants through incentives. Below is a high-level overview of the limited risk liquidity providers take on Futureswap.

Futureswap uses liquidity inside the Futureswap Automated Market Maker (AMM) for trades that are swapped into the Spot AMM (e.g., Uniswap, Fraxswap, etc.). To start, liquidity providers deposit funds into the Futureswap AMM in equal value, similar to adding to other popular AMMs. This liquidity is used for leveraged trades which are swapped back and forth between longs and shorts via the Spot AMM — essentially recycling the liquidity for more trades. Liquidity providers receive trade fees in return for depositing their capital into the protocol.

There are a few items to note about being a Futureswap liquidity provider, but in general, liquidity providers are hedged against trades and therefore delta-neutral.

How is this possible? Let’s go through the flow with an example.

Futureswap’s liquidity providers are automatically engaged into a hedging strategy. When the Futureswap AMM takes the opposite position to a trader, it immediately hedges its position against the Spot AMM with an equivalent position size.

For example, let’s presume a trader takes a 1 ETH long position on Futureswap. The Futureswap AMM then takes a short position of 1 ETH and immediately hedges its position with a long 1 ETH position on the Spot AMM. This means it’s completely delta-neutral and makes the fees with no market exposure.

The only situation where liquidity providers lose is if trades are not liquidated before bankruptcy. This is also the case for most DeFi lending or derivative protocols.

Bankrupt Trades

Just like with any lending platform, the liquidity provider takes a loss when loans that become insolvent are closed.

In this example, presume a trader wants to open a position on the Futureswap ETH-USDC Exchange. The position looks like the following:

Collateral: 10 USDC
Leverage: 10x
Trade Size: 1 ETH
Liquidation Price: $93
Current Price: 1 ETH = 100 USDC

Below is a visual of the different bounds which are set when the trade is open. The trade starts at an open price of $100, and over time the trade moves into the profit range (> $100) or the loss range (< $100).

  • The position is only closable by the trader above a price of $93 (yellow and green sections).
  • If the price is less than $93, anyone can liquidate the position (orange section).
  • If the trade is closed above $90, the liquidity providers receive no loss.
  • If the trade is closed below $90, the liquidity providers take loss (red section).

Bankruptcy almost never precedes liquidation. It can happen if there is an oracle outage (such as Chainlink going down), when the underlying blockchain has issues (for example, an Arbitrum outage), or when there are no liquidators available.

The latter situation (when no liquidators are available) is unlikely because:

  • Liquidators are incentivized to close trades by earning a fee.
  • Anyone can run liquidation bots.
  • We actively monitor positions that are liquidatable and receive alerts.

No-Loss Inconveniences

There are two inconveniences for liquidity providers that can occur in extreme cases:

  • Limited Withdraw
  • Imbalanced Withdraw

In both of these scenarios, liquidity providers’ funds aren’t at risk of losing value. In the worse case, they may not get the same ratio of tokens they put in. Since Futureswap V4 has started in October, the protocol has not seen a scenario where these events have occurred, but we believe they should be noted.

Limited Withdraw

In the case of a Limited Withdraw, the Futureswap AMM is out of balance due to one side being far more popular than the other (too many longs), and the capital from one side has mostly covered over to the other side. Futureswap uses the funding rate to push the Futureswap AMM back into balance for scenarios like this.

For example, let’s consider a Futureswap AMM with Token A and Token B, which starts with 5 of Token A and 50 of Token B. To make the math simpler, let’s assume Token A is $10 and Token B is $1.

Let’s say Bob adds 5 of Token A ($50) and 50 of Token B ($50) for a total value of $100 in his liquidity-providing position. The Futureswap AMM now has a total value of $200 (middle image).

In the third image, the longs vs. shorts ratio is unbalanced. The Futureswap AMM is extremely long Token B.

  • Bob wants to remove liquidity.
  • The maximum Bob can remove is 3 of Token A and 30 of Token B, a total of $60 worth of liquidity.
  • Bob needs to wait until the Futureswap AMM moves back into balance to withdraw his remaining $40.

It’s important to note in this situation no value has been lost for the Futureswap liquidity providers. The only scenario where full withdrawal wouldn’t be possible is when the Futureswap AMM is too unbalanced.

Imbalanced Withdraw

Auto-Deleverage (ADL) is the mechanism by which we allow traders to close their position against other traders when the underlying AMM (e.g., Uniswap) is having issues (e.g., no liquidity). Under normal circumstances, ADL-ing happens against other traders.

In the unlikely event where there are no traders on the other side to ADL against, then the trader closing their position triggers an ADL against the Futureswap AMM. This means that the Futureswap AMM takes a position in stable tokens by selling assets at whatever price the oracle indicates at that time.

ADL-ing against the Futureswap AMM is highly unlikely; most of the time there are traders on both sides — long and short — and ADL occurs between them. This type of situation is called Imbalanced Withdraw, meaning the Futureswap AMM will become slightly off-balance when liquidity providers withdraw at an uneven ratio.

As you can see from the image above, the Futureswap AMM is initially balanced, but after an ADL event against the Futureswap AMM occurs, it becomes slightly uneven. The total value of the liquidity provider position doesn’t change — just the ratio of tokens.

It’s clear why Futureswap is high among the safest markets in which to provide liquidity. There are multiple mechanisms in place — auto-deleveraging and no-loss inconveniences primarily — to protect traders and liquidity providers alike. Nonetheless, for taking on a very limited risk and contributing to the protocol, liquidity providers receive trading fees as a reward. These funds are safe as they’re hedged against traders, making fees with no market exposure. We encourage you to check out the Futureswap public testnet, and to reach out to our team on Discord or Twitter with any questions.

item.title: BTC/ETH Live on Futureswap V4
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
We are excited to announce that you can now trade up to 31x leverage on BTC/ETH with Futureswap V4! Thank you to our supportive community and developers for all of the help and testing that you’ve done.

BTC/ETH is Futureswap’s second exchange. This marks an important turning point where adding new exchanges is now significantly easier. The protocol is now one step closer to being completely permissionless where anyone can list any token pair. This is made possible by keeping each exchange completely isolated from all other exchanges, which at the same time removes the threat of one malicious token being listed and draining other exchanges.

BTC/ETH will allow for many different trading strategies that would not be feasible on a BTC/USDC exchange. The most notable one would be a flippening bet. With ETH as collateral you can deposit ETH and short BTC at 1x thus making a price prediction on ETH’s value flipping everyone’s favorite pet rock. This is much more similar to how Bitmex had BTC as collateral.

D​​ue to BTC/ETH’s correlated nature, Uniswap V3 liquidity will need significantly less active management from LPs (market makers) which will further increase capital efficiency. Liquidity providing will be much more open to everyone and not just active market makers. Ideally, this will attract more liquidity in addition to allowing Futureswap to issue fewer FST incentives to attract an equal amount of liquidity compared to BTC/USDC.

All fees are paid in the collateral of the specific exchange, which means that the Futureswap treasury will be accruing ETH from all trading activity on the BTC/ETH exchange. This treasury is controlled by FST token holders. For more details, see our post on decentralization in Futureswap.

Go check out the new BTC/ETH pool!

Want to stay in the loop? Join us on the Futureswap community Discord and follow us on Twitter.

item.title: Community Update #2
item.dc:creator: Futureswap
item.content:encoded:
Happy holidays from the Futureswap team! We wanted to share a recap of what we’ve been up to since our last community update.

Over the last month, we improved the trader experience by adding Trading View to the chart and launching trade fee incentives, and we started private beta testing a new BTC/ETH pool.

We’ve also hired some new folks, made some community improvements, and more. Read on for more details and other updates!

Stats

  • Total V4 trade volume to date: $215.55m
  • Futureswap LP fees (passive) generated in V4: $120k+
  • Uniswap LP fees (active) generated in V4: $120k+
  • FST distributed over the last 3 months: 1m $FST+

Product

Last week on December 14, we launched Trading View. Dialing in the trading experience has been one of our main priorities since the launch of Futureswap V4 beta. After hearing your feedback, it was clear that having the ability to customize the chart was in high demand.

Some of the key improvements to the chart:

  • You can now create detailed diagrams and charts, similar to the trading experience you may be used to on other exchanges.
  • Candles are now 1H, giving traders more historical context of price movement for assets. We are working on releasing shorter intervals.
  • The issue where the chart display was snapping back after moving it to the desired position has been fixed.

Two weeks ago on December 2, we completed a major upgrade to V4 and released trade fee incentives. Users who make trades now receive FST proportional to the total fees generated in a 24-hour time period.

For the period of December 1 — December 15, the protocol distributed 5,000 FST/day to trade fee incentives. For incentives in the current period and more details, check out the incentives program doc here →

A new BTC/ETH pool is available in a private beta on testnet. We’re excited for the testers to give it a whirl and share feedback with us before we gear up to launch on mainnet.

Governance

Below are some of the recent proposals. Check out the governance forums and governance voting for more.

Mint 500,000 FST for User Incentives
This requested FST to be minted to the rewards DAO for renewing user incentives which includes Futureswap LP, Uniswap v3 LP, Uniswap v2 ETH/FST, trade open interest, and trade fee incentives. This proposal passed. See it here →

Create a WBTC/ETH Exchange
This requested launching an exchange that trades WBTC with ETH collateral. This would need to be wrapped BTC, but done automatically. Profit and loss to be paid out in ETH. The max leverage, which if exceeded, to allow for liquidations, should be 35x, although the frontend will need a lower leverage amount as to not rekt traders instantly upon open. This proposal passed. See it here →

FST Staking (shoutout to Sumoroll)
This is requesting to add FST staking on the protocol in order for holders to earn yield by using the native governance token. This will create a utility for the token other than just governance, and improve tokenomics by locking up tokens and provide additional intrinsic value to the token. This proposal is open and being discussed. See it here →

Launch WBTC/USDC Exchange (shoutout to Caesar)
This is requesting to launch Futureswap v4 on the Uniswap v3 WBTC/USDC 0.3% pool to expand Futureswap’s ecosystem. This proposal is open and being discussed. See it here →

Team

The Futureswap team is growing! In the past month, we had a few new faces join us: kswap on the engineering team and Leisurelord on the community team. Both of them have already made major contributions.

We had a team holiday outing with some family and friends where we got a chance to have some fun and play in VR followed by dinner at a delicious Brazilian steakhouse.

Hiring is hard. It’s taken longer to find the right people for some of the roles than we anticipated. For example, we want to build out a top-notch marketing team that has a deep understanding of DeFi and perps. Guess what? Surprise (not!), it turns out that the pool of people who meet that criteria is pretty small.

We have been exploring different ways to source candidates who might be a good fit while continuing to actively interview candidates in the pipeline, working with recruiters, and reaching out to our network.

Want to help the team grow? Check out our open roles here →

  • Let us know if you’re interested in working with us or have someone you want to send our way.
  • We are offering a $7k referral bounty for anyone you refer that gets hired and stays with Futureswap for at least 6 months.
  • Don’t see an open role, but want to join the team? Shoot us an email at jobs@futureswap.io or message us on Discord.

Community & Social

Leisurelord is in the Futureswamp as our Community Manager! You’ve likely already seen him around the server making memes, answering questions, and generally contributing to the community. He is the community’s chief advocate, serving as the bridge between the community and the team on Discord and Twitter, and keeping things running smoothly.

We hosted our first Discord emoji contest. We’ve run a few meme contests before, but we wanted to try out something different this time and we were blown away. There were so many amazing emojis. Huge thanks to everyone who participated!

Congrats to the winners!

  • 1st place (60 FST): sardrew created :pepefstjump:
  • 2nd place (40 FST): Notgridles created :fstawe:
  • 3rd place (30 FST): igor created :nyanfst:
  • Honorable mention: igor created :30x:
  • Random contest participant (20 FST): DBRolling
  • Random Twitter participant (20 FST): @chainlinkhoe

We now have a Futureswap YouTube channel! We need 100+ subscribers to get a custom channel name and URL. Help us out and subscribe here →

Community calls are now being recorded. Since time zones are still a thing, we want to make sure you can catch the community calls even if you can’t join live. We’re still figuring out the best tools and format for recording these so will make adjustments as we go.

We set up a schedule for community updates. This way you can stay in the loop on what’s going on at Futureswap. You can generally expect:

  • Biweekly community calls on Discord and posted on YouTube
  • Monthly community updates here on our blog

Discord spam improvement. Last month, we implemented emoji reaction roles as a human verification step to prevent spam. It seemed to be doing a decent job, until December 1 when we had an influx of spam bots. We ended up having to temporarily lock new users out while we put a new solution in place. The popular and widely used CAPTCHA.bot is now our verification method of choice.
